newsitem.title: USA: MEHL/Biophile files suit against Palomar.
newsitem.headline: MEHL/Biophile files suit against Palomar.

text.p: MEHL/Biophile International Corp Monday said its Selvac Acquisition Corp unit filed a patent infringement suit against Palomar Medical Technologies Inc seeking to halt Palomar from marketing its laser hair removal products in the U.S.

The suit, filed in a New Jersey district court, alleges that the defendants infringed on the patented method of laser hair removal owned by Nardo Zaias, and exclusively licensed to Mehl's Selvac Acquisition Corp and that the defendants have marketed laser hair removal products before receiving FDA clearance.

The suit was also filed against Palomar subsidiaries Spectrum Medical Technologies Inc, Spectrum Financial Services LLC, and a New Jersey dermatologist, for patent infringement and unfair competition, MEHL said.
The plaintiff is seeking monetary damages and injunctive relief to restrain Palomar from marketing its products.
MEHL said its long pulse ruby hair removal system is protected by patents, both granted and pending, in the U.S.

A spokesman for Palomar, which today said it received U.S. Fodd and Drug Administration approval to market its EpiLaser hair removal system, denied that the company is infringing on the patent in question.

"We have thoroughly and laboriously reseached the possibility of infringing on the Zaias patent and we are absolutely confident that we are not doing so," said John Ingoldsby, Palomar's director of investor relations. "We believe their suit has absolutely no merit," he said.
